faqs.question: Which short Diwali line can a Class 2 child write in the school diary?
faqs.answer: Pick one under eight words with a single picture word, such as "My diya is little. My light is not." or "I lit a diya and it smiled back." Older classes can take longer lines, up to about 25 words for Classes 9–12, and every line on this page is original.

faqs.question: Which Diwali quote suits a school assembly thought for the day?
faqs.answer: Pick a line of about 20 words that lands when heard once, such as "One diya cannot light a city, but it has never refused to try." For Diwali week 2027, a school open until Thursday has four assembly mornings, Monday 25 to Thursday 28 October, so this page gives one thought for each.

faqs.question: How long should a Diwali quote for a school notice board be?
faqs.answer: Keep it to about eight words for Classes 1–3 and 15 words for older classes. A notice board is read on paper from a metre or two away while people walk past, so one picture word such as diya or rangoli and one idea is enough.

faqs.question: Is "tamaso ma jyotirgamaya" a Diwali quote?
faqs.answer: It is not written about Diwali, but it is widely used because it asks to be led from darkness to light. It comes from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad (I.3.28), where it is one of three verses recited at a Vedic sacrifice; F. Max Müller's 1884 translation reads "Lead me from darkness to light!" Name that source when a student reads it out.

faqs.question: What is a good eco-friendly Diwali quote for students?
faqs.answer: "Light the room, not the lungs." works on an eco-club poster because a 2026 study of 14 Indo-Gangetic Basin cities in Scientific Reports found Diwali PM2.5 and PM10 at 3–10 times the 24-hour limits, with Delhi's PM2.5 up 19% over the festival. Pair the line with that number.

faqs.question: How loud are firecrackers allowed to be in India?
faqs.answer: India's Central Pollution Control Board standard, notified in 1999 under the Environment (Protection) Rules, bans the manufacture, sale or use of crackers louder than 125 dB(AI) at 4 metres from where they burst. That figure makes a factual safety-corner line: "125 decibels is the legal ceiling at four metres. A diya stays at zero."

faqs.question: When is Diwali 2027, and when should schools use these quotes?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja falls on Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 and Choti Diwali on Thursday 28 October. For a school open until Thursday, Monday 25 to Thursday 28 October is the window for assembly lines and notice boards.

faqs.question: What Diwali quote fits Class 10 students before board exams?
faqs.answer: A line that gives permission to rest works best, such as "Rest is not a break from the syllabus. It is part of it." Keep it under 25 words so it fits a phone screen in the class group, where 48.3% of SubhSandesh shared pages are opened on a phone.

faqs.question: Can students use these quotes in a Diwali essay or speech competition?
faqs.answer: Use them as models, not as the entry. If the competition asks for the student's own writing, write a fresh line with one picture and one verb, and name the source of any classical line, such as the 1884 Max Müller translation of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

faqs.question: How can a student send a Diwali quote to a friend who moved to another city?
faqs.answer: Write the quote into a card or a page made for that one friend. SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali page holds one line in each wish diya, a rangoli with initials and a letter in a liffafa, takes about five minutes, and opens in any browser with no app; a younger child should build it with a parent, who sends the private link.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Quotes for Students, Sorted by Class and by Where They Go

Diwali quotes for students work when the length matches the class and the place the line will be read: under eight words for Classes 1–3, one sentence for Classes 4–8, and a line with a turn in it for Classes 9–12. Below are 30 original diwali quotes in English for students, plus one classical line with its real source. For a class WhatsApp group, write for a phone: on SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone (27,725 of 57,456 views, measured 24 September 2026). Lines also get reread; the average SubhSandesh page is viewed 11.1 times, so pick one that holds up on the third look.

Diwali 2027 falls on Friday 29 October; below are lines by class, a thought for each assembly morning, and eco and safety lines with numbers.

## What makes a Diwali quote work for students?

A Diwali quote for students is a short, self-contained line about light, effort or care that a child can read, say aloud or pin up without explanation. Unlike a wish, it speaks to a whole room, not one person.

School is where these lines get used. A [Delhi Directorate of Education circular dated 16 October 2019](https://www.edudel.nic.in/upload/upload_2019_20/891_dt_16102019.PDF) told school heads to personally address the morning assembly on eco-friendly ways to celebrate, and asked each eco-club to carry the message to students and parents. The assembly line, the notice board and the eco-club poster are three jobs needing three lengths.

## Diwali quotes in English for students, class by class

Each band gives the length, where the line goes, and original lines; swap in a class or teacher's name.

### Classes 1–3: under eight words, for the notice board

Length: four to eight words, readable in one breath. Where: the class display board, a drawing, or the first line in the school diary. One picture word (diya, rangoli, mithai) makes a line a six-year-old can copy and claim.

- "My diya is little. My light is not."
- "Dear diya, thank you for being so quiet."
- "I lit a diya and it smiled back."
- "Rangoli colours on my hands all day."
- "Lights on, voices soft, hearts full."

### Classes 4–5: one full sentence, for a card or the class board

Length: one sentence of 10 to 15 words. Where: a handmade card, the class board, or a line read before the prayer. A line can now hold a small idea, not only a picture.

- "A diya never asks whose house it is lighting."
- "Hold a lamp up for a friend and your own road gets brighter."
- "Ask Dadi how she spent Diwali at your age; that story is the gift."
- "My rangoli will be swept away tomorrow, and I am still making it carefully."

### Classes 6–8: a line with a twist, for the assembly or the class group

Length: up to 20 words, with a turn halfway through. Where: the assembly anchor's closing line, the class group run by a parent or class teacher, or a chart-paper heading.

- "Darkness is only a room waiting for someone to find the switch."
- "Ram took fourteen years to get home. Your project is due Monday. You've got this."
- "A firecracker shines for two seconds. A good habit shines all year."
- "Share your notes the way a diya shares its flame: nothing lost, everything brighter."

### Classes 9–10: the board-exam year

Length: under 25 words. Where: the class group, a status, or a card to a study partner. Months before boards, the useful line permits rest without dropping the work.

- "Rest is not a break from the syllabus. It is part of it."
- "Light one diya for the chapters you finished and one for the chapters you will."
- "Revision is Diwali cleaning for the mind: slow, dusty and worth it."

### Classes 11–12 and first-year college

Length: up to 25 words. Where: a status, an entrance-exam study group, or a note to a younger sibling.

- "A career is built on a hundred ordinary evenings, not one bright night. Enjoy this one anyway."
- "The lamp doesn't know it is beating the dark. It just keeps burning. Study like that."
- "Call the friend who explained physics to you at midnight. Light travels both ways."

## A thought for the day for each school day before the break

With Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October 2027, a school open until Thursday has four assembly mornings left in Diwali week, Monday 25 to Thursday 28 October. One thought for each, with the sentence the anchor reads after it:

- **Monday 25 October:** "One diya cannot light a city, but it has never refused to try." Read after: small effort counts, even when the job is big.
- **Tuesday 26 October:** "Rangoli blows away by morning, and people still make it with care." Read after: do good work even when it won't last.
- **Wednesday 27 October (Dhanteras):** "Dhanteras is about wealth. The kind no thief can take is what you learn." Read after: knowledge is the wealth you keep.
- **Thursday 28 October (Choti Diwali):** the classical line below.

> "Lead me from the unreal to the real! Lead me from darkness to light! Lead me from death to immortality!" Brihadaranyaka Upanishad I.3.28, translated by F. Max Müller, *The Sacred Books of the East*, Vol. 15, 1884 ([Internet Archive scan](https://archive.org/details/wg915)).
> तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय (tamaso mā jyotir gamaya): "Lead me from darkness to light."

Tamas means darkness and also ignorance, which is why it suits a school. In the text it is one of three verses recited at a Vedic sacrifice; assembly use is modern.

## Eco and safety Diwali quotes for students, with the numbers behind them

Eco-club posters work better when a line carries a real number. Two are worth printing.

First, air. A [study of 14 Indo-Gangetic Basin cities in *Scientific Reports* (23 June 2026)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13574772) found PM2.5 and PM10 during Diwali exceeded the 24-hour limits of India's Central Pollution Control Board and the WHO by 3–10 times, with Delhi's PM2.5 rising 19% over the festival. The CPCB's 24-hour PM2.5 limit is 60 µg/m³.

Second, noise. The [CPCB noise standard for fire-crackers](https://cpcb.gov.in/displaypdf.php?id=bm9pc2VsaW1pdF9maXJlY3JhY2tlcnMucGRm), notified in 1999 under the Environment (Protection) Rules, bans the manufacture, sale or use of crackers louder than 125 dB(AI) at 4 metres from the point of bursting.

For the eco-club board:

- "Light the room, not the lungs."
- "125 decibels is the legal ceiling at four metres. A diya stays at zero."
- "Breathe in. That air belongs to your neighbour too."
- "The best Diwali sound is Nani laughing, not a bomb two streets away."
- "A clay diya crumbles into soil. Cracker paper just sits in the drain."

For the safety corner:

- "Cotton on, synthetic off, and a grown-up within reach."
- "A sparkler is a tiny fire on a stick. Hold it like one."
- "Hurt hands can't hold a pen after the holidays."

## Notice board, assembly, class group or card: compared

Each place a student quote goes has its own word limit. This table compares four, with one figure that applies to each:

| Where the quote goes | Word cap used on this page | How it is read | Figure that applies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notice board or chart paper | 8 words (Classes 1–3), 15 above | Paper, from a metre or two, in passing | CPCB limit worth printing: 125 dB(AI) at 4 m |
| Morning assembly | 20 words, one breath | Heard once by the whole school | Delhi DoE circular, 16 October 2019: heads asked to address assembly |
| Class WhatsApp group | 25 words, one screen | On a parent's or student's phone | 48.3% of SubhSandesh shared pages opened on a phone |
| Card or page for one classmate | A quote plus two sentences | One person, more than once | 11.1 views per SubhSandesh page on average |

The shorter the time a line is seen, the fewer words it gets: an assembly line is heard once, while a page for one friend can carry a longer note.

## Where SubhSandesh fits, and the one person it is for

A notice board and an assembly need no link. A Diwali page is for one person a student misses, such as a classmate who moved city or a grandparent who cannot visit.

For that person, SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card with diyas, rangoli and a shagun liffafa](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) lets a student put one quote into each wish diya. The recipient lights a diya at their door, colours a rangoli until the initials glow, and opens a letter from a red-and-gold liffafa; its crackers are drawn, with no noise or smoke. It takes about five minutes; younger children should build it with a parent, who sends the private link, and it opens in any browser with no app.

For two best friends in the same class, [the Capsule page, where two people seal predictions for a year](https://subhsandesh.in/capsule) fits better. It is not a Diwali template: each friend writes guesses blind to the other, and it opens a year later, around Diwali 2028, to score them.

No Diwali data exists yet. In Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest analogue (n = 89 pages), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself, so start by Thursday 28 October.

## When a Diwali quote is the wrong thing for a student to share

A borrowed quote is wrong inside graded work. If a Diwali essay or speech competition asks for the student's own writing, a line from this page belongs in the student's notebook as a model, not in the entry; write a fresh one with one picture and one verb.

A quote is also wrong as a way round a quarrel. If two friends fell out before the break, a forwarded line dodges the sorry; saying it in person on Govardhan Puja, Saturday 30 October, does the job. Where a school restricts phones on campus, any link belongs at home, and a handmade card on the class teacher's desk beats one.

## Sources

- Directorate of Education, Govt. of NCT of Delhi. Circular No. DE.23 (619)/Sch.Br./2019/891, "Anti Fire Crackers Campaign", 16 October 2019.
- Bartaria V. et al. "Firecracker-induced air pollution and health burden during Diwali" (14 Indo-Gangetic Basin cities). *Scientific Reports* 16, 28665, 23 June 2026.
- Central Pollution Control Board. "Noise Standards for Fire-crackers", G.S.R. 682(E), 5 October 1999.
- F. Max Müller (tr.). *The Upanishads, Part II*, Sacred Books of the East Vol. 15, 1884 (public domain).
